extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, practitioners, and USPTO examiners
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive requirements for filing, recognizing, and processing an express abandonment (and related petitions) under 37 CFR 1.138 (including petitions to avoid publication and for refund of search/excess claims fees). Guidance covers form use, timing, signatures, filing channels, and effects after payment of issue fee or during interferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness requires recognition and action by USPTO
rubrics_metrics.description: A paper requesting express abandonment of an application is not effective unless and until an appropriate USPTO official recognizes and acts on the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action in recognition may take the form of an acknowledgement by the Publishing Division indicating compliance with 37 CFR 1.138. The paper will not stop publication unless recognized and acted on by the Pre-Grant Publication Division in sufficient time to avoid publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing channels and recommended transmission methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of express abandonment or petitions under 37 CFR 1.138(c)/(d) and related petitions/fees may be mailed to Mail Stop Express Abandonment or transmitted by facsimile to the Pre-Grant Publication Division; petitions to withdraw from issue should be addressed to the Office of Petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When projected publication date is less than 3 months from petition date, applicants should transmit the petition by facsimile to increase chance of timely recognition. For petitions after payment of issue fee, applicants are strongly encouraged to either fax or hand-carry the petition to allow sufficient time to process and, if granted, withdraw the application from issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express abandonment after payment of issue fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter of express abandonment is submitted after payment of the issue fee, it must be accompanied by a petition to withdraw from issue under 37 CFR 1.313(c) and the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition will not be effective unless actually received and granted by appropriate official before the date of issue. After issue fee payment, an application will not be withdrawn on petition except for reasons listed in 37 CFR 1.313(c), including express abandonment. If 1.313 precludes effect, the appropriate remedy may be a petition under 37 CFR 1.183 showing extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing to avoid publication (37 CFR 1.138(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition under 37 CFR 1.138(c) to avoid publication will be granted only if recognized in sufficient time to avoid publication; generally it must be received more than four weeks prior to the projected date of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is unlikely a petition filed within four weeks of projected publication will be effective. Use of form PTO/SB/24A and facsimile to Pre-Grant Publication Division (703-305-8568) is recommended for petitions to avoid publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund of search fee and excess claims fee (37 CFR 1.138(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain refund of the search fee and excess claims fee under 37 CFR 1.138(d), the petition and declaration of express abandonment must be submitted before an examination has been made of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date on any certificate of mailing or transmission under § 1.8 is not taken into account for determining whether the petition was filed before examination. If not filed before examination, the Office will not refund except as provided in § 1.26. A petition under 1.138(d) will be denied if PALM shows status higher than 031 on or before the filing day; technical preparations for publication generally begin four months prior to projected publication date. Form PTO/SB/24B is recommended; facsimile to Pre-Grant Publication is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'examination has been made' for 1.138(d)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'An examination has been made of the application' once an action (e.g., restriction/election requirement, requirement for information under 37 CFR 1.105, first Office action on the merits, notice of allowability or allowance, action under Ex parte Quayle) is shown in PALM as having been counted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition and an action are both counted on the same day, the petition was not filed before an examination. PALM status higher than 031 on or before filing day results in denial of 1.138(d) petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form use and purposes (PTO/SB/24, 24A, 24B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/24 may be used for filing a letter of express abandonment; PTO/SB/24A for petition under 1.138(c) to avoid publication; PTO/SB/24B for petition under 1.138(d) to obtain a refund of search fee and excess claims fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms include required fields and signature blocks; use of the specific form suited to the requested relief is recommended to avoid delays. The MPEP reproduces these forms and recommends their use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature and signature-count requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Signature of all the inventors or assignees of record of the entire interest or their representative(s) are required on express abandonment forms; submit multiple forms if more than one signature is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In interferences, an abandonment signed only by an attorney or agent of record is not effective to terminate the interference; to be effective to terminate an interference, abandonment must be signed by the inventor with written consent of the assignee where there has been an assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Untimely letters of express abandonment (outside reply period)
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of express abandonment which is not timely filed (because it was not filed within the period for reply) is not acceptable to expressly abandon the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such letters should be placed in the application file but not formally entered. The application should be pulled for abandonment after expiration of the maximum permitted period for reply and applicant notified of abandonment for failure to reply within the statutory period (see MPEP §§ 711.02, 711.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments canceling all claims are not express abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment canceling all of the claims, even though signed by applicant and assignee, is not an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will not enter any amendment that would cancel all of the claims without presenting any new or substitute claims; such an amendment is regarded as nonresponsive and not a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action. The practice in 37 CFR 1.135(c) does not apply to such amendments; applicant should be notified as explained in MPEP § 714.03 to § 714.05.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of appeal by non-of-record attorney may effect abandonment
rubrics_metrics.description: An attorney or agent not of record may file a withdrawal of an appeal under 37 CFR 1.34(a) except where such withdrawal would result in abandonment of the application; in such instances the withdrawal of appeal is in fact an express abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When withdrawal would result in abandonment, the filing by a non-of-record attorney or agent operates as an express abandonment; special care in these situations is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement and Notice of Abandonment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a letter expressly abandoning the application complies with 37 CFR 1.138, Office personnel should respond using a 'Notice of Abandonment' form PTO-1432 and check the appropriate box(es). If the letter does not comply, a fully explanatory letter should be sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acknowledgment by the Publishing Division indicating compliance with 37 CFR 1.138 is an example of action in recognition of express abandonment; such acknowledgement increases certainty that the abandonment will be effective as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional application consideration before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: It is suggested that divisional applications be reviewed before filing to ascertain whether the prior application should be abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care should be exercised when considering express abandonment in favor of a continuing/divisional application because the Office looks on express abandonments as acts of deliberation intentionally performed.
